text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Talks between Greek and Turkish Cypriot sides in Montreux on Monday focused on security, territorial issues and human rights. Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash demanded suspension of Cyprus's EU membership bid and halt to purchase of Russian S300 missile system.
- Government tries to steer economy towards expanding into other sectors like health and education.
- Round two. U.N. envoy Diego Cordovez admits he is not expecting settlement to Cyprus problem from five days of talks, but sees process as step towards possible solution.
- British tourists sue five British squaddies over Ayia Napa night club attack.
- Six hundred Greek Cypriots due to make their first pilgrimage in 23 years to Turkish-held monastery of Apostolos Andreas in north.
- Montreux talks start under media blackout. Diego Cordovez says new methods need to be adopted in approach to talks.
- Licensed porters in Limassol port will start laying off staff after summer holidays as work cycle of port gets smaller.
- Michael Jackson due to hold concert at Limassol's Tsirion stadium in October.
- President Clerides raises basic principles that a Cyprus settlement should be based on during first day of Montreux talks.
- U.N. resident envoy in Cyprus Gustave Feissel excluded from first round of talks.
